papers.title: scMustree: a multi-scale functional hierarchy for single-cell transcriptomic analysis
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Resolving cellular heterogeneity requires methods that capture both discrete cell types and their functional relationships. Existing single-cell clustering approaches often produce flat partitions, limiting their ability to reveal rare cell states and continuous biological transitions. Here, we introduce scMustree, a computational framework that constructs a multi-scale hierarchy of single-cell transcriptomes, enabling integrated analysis of cellular organization and functional relationships. scMustree employs a top-down iterative decomposition to isolate transcriptionally homogeneous populations, followed by a bottom-up merging strategy guided by cluster-specific functional rankings—derived from differential expression and an isolation-forest-based scoring mechanism that quantifies functional distinctness. This unified approach captures lineage structures, functional similarities, and transitional states. Results Across 11 benchmark datasets, scMustree achieves competitive clustering accuracy while offering substantially enhanced biological interpretability. In diverse biological systems, it uncovers biologically consistent hierarchies and identifies previously uncharacterized cell states, including fibroblast and T-cell subsets in cancer and lipid-associated microglial populations in Alzheimer’s disease. By integrating structural and functional information, scMustree provides a scalable and biologically grounded framework for multi-resolution exploration of single-cell ecosystems, enabling discovery of rare and disease-relevant cell states across diverse biological contexts. Availability and implementation Freely available at Github( https://github.com/xuyp-csu/scMustree ) and Zenodo( https://zenodo.org/records/17480562 )

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：要解决细胞间的异质性问题，就必须采用能够同时识别不同类型的细胞及其功能关系的研究方法。
llm_highlights_zh: 现有的单细胞聚类方法通常会产生扁平的聚类结果，这限制了它们揭示稀有细胞状态及连续生物学变化的能力。
在这里，我们介绍 scMustree——这一计算框架能够构建单细胞转录组的多尺度层次结构，从而实现对细胞组织结构与功能关系的综合分析。
scMustree采用自上而下的迭代分解方法来分离那些在转录水平上具有高度一致性的细胞群体，随后再通过自下而上的合并策略进行整合。这一合并过程依据通过差异表达分析得出的各簇细胞的功能重要性排序来进行指导，并且还运用基于“隔离森林”算法的评分机制来量化这些细胞群在功能上的差异程度。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
要理解细胞间的异质性，就必须同时捕捉不同的细胞类型及其功能关系。现有的单细胞聚类方法往往生成扁平的群体结构，这限制了它们揭示稀有细胞状态及连续生物学过程的能力。为此，我们提出了scMustree这一计算框架——该框架能够构建多尺度的单细胞转录组层次结构，从而实现细胞组织与功能关系的综合分析。scMustree首先采用自上而下的迭代分解方法分离出转录特征相似的细胞群体，随后通过自下而上的合并策略，结合基于差异表达数据得出的簇特异性功能排序结果，以及一种能够量化功能差异性的评分机制，最终形成完整的层次结构。这种统一的方法有效揭示了细胞的谱系关系、功能相似性及过渡状态。  

**实验结果**  
在11个基准数据集上的测试表明，scMustree不仅具有较高的聚类准确率，其生物学解释性也得到了显著提升。在多种生物系统中，该工具均能揭示出具有生物学意义的层次结构，并识别出此前未被描述的细胞类型——例如癌症中的成纤维细胞和T细胞亚群，以及阿尔茨海默病中与脂质相关的小胶质细胞群体。通过整合结构信息与功能数据，scMustree为多尺度探索单细胞生态系统提供了可扩展且基于生物学原理的分析工具，有助于在多种生物背景下发现稀有或与疾病相关的细胞状态。  

**开源与使用方式**  
scMustree已免费发布在Github（https://github.com/xuyp-csu/scMustree）和Zenodo（https://zenodo.org/records/17480562）平台上，可供大家自由下载和使用。

MOTIVATION: Resolving cellular heterogeneity requires methods that capture both discrete cell types and their functional relationships. Existing single-cell clustering approaches often produce flat partitions, limiting their ability to reveal rare cell states and continuous biological transitions. Here, we introduce scMustree, a computational framework that constructs a multi-scale hierarchy of single-cell transcriptomes, enabling integrated analysis of cellular organization and functional relationships. scMustree employs a top-down iterative decomposition to isolate transcriptionally homogeneous populations, followed by a bottom-up merging strategy guided by cluster-specific functional rankings-derived from differential expression and an isolation-forest-based scoring mechanism that quantifies functional distinctness. This unified approach captures lineage structures, functional similarities, and transitional states.

RESULTS: Across 11 benchmark datasets, scMustree achieves competitive clustering accuracy while offering substantially enhanced biological interpretability. In diverse biological systems, it uncovers biologically consistent hierarchies and identifies previously uncharacterized cell states, including fibroblast and T-cell subsets in cancer and lipid-associated microglial populations in Alzheimer's disease. By integrating structural and functional information, scMustree provides a scalable and biologically grounded framework for multi-resolution exploration of single-cell ecosystems, enabling discovery of rare and disease-relevant cell states across diverse biological contexts.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: Freely available at Github(https://github.com/xuyp-csu/scMustree) and Zenodo(https://zenodo.org/records/17480562).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.title: Phys-AbGAT: A Physics-Informed Multi-Task Graph Attention Network for Robust Antibody-Antigen Binding Affinity Prediction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity is essential for therapeutic antibody design. Existing methods often model the dissociation constant (KD) and Gibbs free energy (ΔG) independently, overlooking their thermodynamic relationship and complex paratope-epitope spatial interactions. Results We introduce Phys-AbGAT, a physics-informed multi-task graph attention network that represents the antibody-antigen interface as a spatial graph. It integrates ESM2 evolutionary embeddings with radial basis functions and employs a thermodynamically motivated auxiliary loss to encourage coupling between log10⁡(KD) and ΔG. On an independent 42-complex benchmark, Phys-AbGAT achieved Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.569 for log10⁡(KD) and 0.573 for ΔG. In matched-set comparisons, Phys-AbGAT achieved numerically lower RMSE and higher PCC than four baseline methods. The differences remained significant after Holm correction for MVSF-AB and PPA-Pred2, but not for AREA-AFFINITY or CSM-AB. Higher attention scores were assigned to several aromatic paratope residues, providing model-level hypotheses for structural inspection. These results support Phys-AbGAT as an interpretable multi-task geometric framework for joint prediction of two affinity-related quantities. Availability and implementation Code and data are available at https://github.com/cliffgao/Phys-AbGAT

llm_highlights_zh: 现有方法通常将解离常数（KD）与吉布斯自由能（ΔG）视为独立的参数进行建模，忽略了它们之间的热力学关系以及抗原表位与抗体结合部位之间复杂的空间相互作用。

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
准确预测抗体与抗原之间的结合亲和力对于治疗性抗体的设计至关重要。现有方法通常分别独立地建模解离常数（KD）和吉布斯自由能（ΔG），而忽略了它们之间的热力学关系以及复杂的抗原表位-抗体表位空间相互作用。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了Phys-AbGAT这一基于物理原理的多任务图注意力网络模型。该模型将抗体-抗原界面表示为一种空间结构，并结合了ESM2进化嵌入技术与径向基函数；同时，通过引入热力学驱动的辅助损失函数，促进log10(KD)与ΔG之间的耦合关系。在针对42种复合物的独立测试中，Phys-AbGAT分别获得了0.569和0.573的皮尔逊相关系数。在与其他四种基线方法的对比中，Phys-AbGAT在均方根误差（RMSE）和匹配度指标（PCC）上均表现出更优的性能；即使经过Holm校正后，MVSF-AB与PPA-Pred2之间的差异仍然显著，而AREA-AFFINITY与CSM-AB则没有这种差异。此外，该模型为某些芳香族抗原表位残基赋予了更高的权重，这些结果为进一步分析抗体结构提供了理论依据。  

**代码与数据获取方式**  
相关代码及数据可访问以下链接：https://github.com/cliffgao/Phys-AbGAT

papers.title: Partaker: deep-learning-based single-cell-resolution analysis of multi-dimensional, long-term, microfluidic-based time-lapse microscopy data
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Deep-learning segmentation models for microbial time-lapse fluorescence microscopy already exist, but they are often difficult to use consistently across experiments and are not packaged with unified workflows for combining models, quantifying multi-channel fluorescence, and scaling analyses to large microfluidic imaging datasets. Results To address these challenges, we developed Partaker, an easy-to-use Python-based graphical tool for deep-learning segmentation, multi-channel fluorescence quantification, and morphological analysis of microbial cells over time. Partaker supports extensible model integration, efficient handling of large imaging datasets, and interactive visualization, enabling time-resolved analysis of population fluorescence distributions from per-cell measurements. We demonstrate performance using a two-strain validation experiment (housekeeping and inducible) and show robust recovery of population-level fluorescence dynamics with single-cell resolution. Availability and implementation Partaker is implemented in Python and is available on GitHub ( https://github.com/SamOliveiraLab/partaker ). A versioned release of the software is archived on Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18844425 ). Documentation, example datasets, and installation instructions are provided in the repository

目前已有用于微生物时间序列荧光显微镜成像的深度学习分割模型，但这些模型在不同实验中往往难以被一致地应用，且缺乏统一的工作流程来整合这些模型、量化多通道荧光信号，或将分析方法扩展到大规模微流控成像数据集。为解决这些问题，我们开发了Partaker——这一基于Python的可视化工具，能够便捷地实现微生物细胞的深度学习分割、多通道荧光信号的定量分析以及形态学研究。Partaker支持模型的灵活集成，能够高效处理大规模图像数据，并提供交互式可视化功能，从而实现对细胞群体荧光分布的时序分析。我们通过包含两种菌株的验证实验来证明其性能，结果表明该工具能够以单细胞分辨率准确还原群体层面的荧光动态变化。

papers.title: HiCPotts: An R/Bioconductor package to identify significant interactions in chromosome conformation capture data and model sources of bias
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Chromosome Conformation Capture methods, including Hi-C, micro-C or Capture-C, are used to map chromatin interactions genome-wide. Most of the existing computational methods do not account for sources of bias (such as DNA accessibility, GC content or TE content) in the data. Results We previously developed ZipHiC, a Bayesian method based on the hidden Markov random field (HMRF) model and the Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC), that uses zero-inflated Poisson distribution to model the noise, signal and false signal of the data and showed that this approach was able to detect bias from DNA accessibility, GC content and TE content in both Hi-C and micro-C data. Here, we present HiCPotts, another Bayesian method based on the HMRF model and the ABC that uses a zero-inflated Negative Binomial distribution instead to model the noise and signal of the data. We systematically show that HiCPotts reduces false positives and increases recovery of true interactions compared to ZipHiC, but also compared to other methods such as FastHiC, Juicer and HiCExplorer. Most importantly, we provide an R/Bioconductor package that allows modelling the noise, signal and false signal using various distributions such as the zero-inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) and the zero-inflated Poisson distribution (ZIP). Availability and Implementation https://bioconductor.org/packages/HiCPotts/

papers.title: Gradient-based Optimization for mRNA Sequence Design
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Designing mRNA coding sequences that simultaneously optimize RNA accessibility in the translation initiation region and codon adaptation while preserving the encoded protein requires navigating a vast discrete combinatorial space. The inherently discrete nature of codon choices prevents direct application of gradient-based optimization, despite the availability of accurate deep learning predictors such as DeepRaccess for RNA accessibility prediction. Results We present the Input Data Differentiable Designer (ID3), a unified framework for mRNA codon optimization. ID3 treats trained models as fixed differentiable functions and optimizes input data through continuous probability distributions while preserving the encoded amino acid sequence through three constraint mechanisms. The framework shows strong performance in both accessibility optimization and joint accessibility-CAI optimization across diverse protein targets. We also provide convergence analyses from the perspective of trained model input optimization. ID3将训练好的模型视为可微分的固定函数，通过连续概率分布来优化输入数据；同时，它利用三种约束机制来确保编码后的氨基酸序列不会发生改变。

papers.title: Causal Spectral Segmenter: Counterfactual Graph Reasoning for Weakly Supervised Pathology Segmentation
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Weakly supervised pathology segmentation aims to alleviate the reliance on costly pixel-level annotations, yet remains challenging due to severe tissue heterogeneity, complex morphological patterns, and strong contextual confounding in histopathology images. Existing transformer-based methods often learn spurious correlations between lesions and surrounding tissues, while graph-based approaches tend to suffer from feature over-smoothing, resulting in degraded boundary delineation and localization accuracy. Results To address these challenges, we propose a novel Causal Spectral Segmenter (CSS) for weakly supervised pathology segmentation. The proposed framework seamlessly integrates causal representation learning and multi-scale spectral graph reasoning. Specifically, a Causal Counterfactual Projector (CCP) is introduced to estimate lesion-specific causal effects through factual–counterfactual intervention, thereby suppressing contextual confounding and enhancing lesion-discriminative representations. Furthermore, we develop a Multi-scale Spectral Graph Reasoner (MSGR) composed of stacked Spectral Chebyshev Graph Convolution (SCGC) layers, which perform topology-aware spectral propagation across multiple neighborhood scales to capture long-range tissue dependencies while mitigating graph over-smoothing. By jointly modeling causal effects and multi-scale topological structures, CSS effectively improves lesion localization and boundary preservation under weak supervision. Extensive experiments on two public histopathology segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that CSS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods and achieves superior segmentation accuracy and structural consistency. Availability and Implementation The source code and implementation details will be publicly available at: https://github.com/zhangxu90s/CSS

所提出的框架将因果表示学习与多尺度谱图推理无缝结合在一起。

在弱监督病理分割领域，虽然人们试图减少对昂贵像素级标注的依赖，但由于组织结构的异质性、复杂的形态特征以及组织病理图像中的强烈背景干扰，这一目标仍面临诸多挑战。现有的基于Transformer的方法往往会学习到病变与周围组织之间的虚假关联，而基于图论的方法则容易出现特征过度平滑的问题，从而导致边界划分和定位精度下降。  

**研究方法**  
为了解决这些难题，我们提出了一种新型的因果谱段分割算法——CSS。该框架将因果关系表示学习与多尺度谱图推理有机结合在一起：首先引入了因果反事实投影器（CCP），通过事实与反事实干预来估计病变特有的因果效应，从而有效抑制背景干扰并提升病变的区分能力；随后构建了由多层谱切比雪夫图卷积层组成的多尺度谱图推理器（MSGR），该机制能够在多个不同尺度上实现基于拓扑结构的谱传播，既能捕捉组织间的长距离依赖关系，又能避免特征过度平滑。通过同时建模因果效应与多尺度拓扑结构，CSS在弱监督环境下显著提升了病变的定位精度与边界保持能力。  

**实验验证**  
在两个公开发布的组织病理分割基准测试中，CSS的表现明显优于现有最先进方法，其分割精度与结构一致性均得到了显著提升。  

**代码与实现**

papers.primary_summary_raw: Weakly supervised pathology segmentation aims to alleviate the reliance on costly pixel-level annotations, yet remains challenging due to severe tissue heterogeneity, complex morphological patterns, and strong contextual confounding in histopathology images. Existing transformer-based methods often learn spurious correlations between lesions and surrounding tissues, while graph-based approaches tend to suffer from feature over-smoothing, resulting in degraded boundary delineation and localization accuracy. Results To address these challenges, we propose a novel Causal Spectral Segmenter (CSS) for weakly supervised pathology segmentation. The proposed framework seamlessly integrates causal representation learning and multi-scale spectral graph reasoning. Specifically, a Causal Counterfactual Projector (CCP) is introduced to estimate lesion-specific causal effects through factual–counterfactual intervention, thereby suppressing contextual confounding and enhancing lesion-discriminative representations. Furthermore, we develop a Multi-scale Spectral Graph Reasoner (MSGR) composed of stacked Spectral Chebyshev Graph Convolution (SCGC) layers, which perform topology-aware spectral propagation across multiple neighborhood scales to capture long-range tissue dependencies while mitigating graph over-smoothing. By jointly modeling causal effects and multi-scale topological structures, CSS effectively improves lesion localization and boundary preservation under weak supervision. Extensive experiments on two public histopathology segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that CSS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods and achieves superior segmentation accuracy and structural consistency.

all_papers.title: HiCPotts: An R/Bioconductor package to identify significant interactions in chromosome conformation capture data and model sources of bias
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Chromosome Conformation Capture methods, including Hi-C, micro-C or Capture-C, are used to map chromatin interactions genome-wide. Most of the existing computational methods do not account for sources of bias (such as DNA accessibility, GC content or TE content) in the data. Results We previously developed ZipHiC, a Bayesian method based on the hidden Markov random field (HMRF) model and the Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC), that uses zero-inflated Poisson distribution to model the noise, signal and false signal of the data and showed that this approach was able to detect bias from DNA accessibility, GC content and TE content in both Hi-C and micro-C data. Here, we present HiCPotts, another Bayesian method based on the HMRF model and the ABC that uses a zero-inflated Negative Binomial distribution instead to model the noise and signal of the data. We systematically show that HiCPotts reduces false positives and increases recovery of true interactions compared to ZipHiC, but also compared to other methods such as FastHiC, Juicer and HiCExplorer. Most importantly, we provide an R/Bioconductor package that allows modelling the noise, signal and false signal using various distributions such as the zero-inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) and the zero-inflated Poisson distribution (ZIP). Availability and Implementation https://bioconductor.org/packages/HiCPotts/

RESULTS: We previously developed ZipHiC, a Bayesian method based on the hidden Markov random field (HMRF) model and the Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC), that uses zero-inflated Poisson distribution to model the noise, signal and false signal of the data and showed that this approach was able to detect bias from DNA accessibility, GC content and TE content in both Hi-C and micro-C data. Here, we present HiCPotts, another Bayesian method based on the HMRF model and the ABC that uses a zero-inflated Negative Binomial distribution instead to model the noise and signal of the data. all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
摘要  
动机：染色体构象捕获技术（如Hi-C、micro-C或Capture-C）被用于全基因组范围内研究染色质相互作用。然而，现有的大多数计算方法并未考虑数据中存在的各种偏差因素（例如DNA的可及性、GC含量或TE含量等）。  

结果：我们此前开发了ZipHiC——这是一种基于隐马尔可夫随机场模型与近似贝叶斯计算方法的贝叶斯算法，该算法使用零膨胀泊松分布来模拟数据中的噪声、真实信号以及假阳性信号。实验结果表明，这种方法能够有效识别Hi-C及micro-C数据中由DNA可及性、GC含量等因素引起的偏差。在此研究中，我们进一步提出了HiCPotts——这一同样基于隐马尔可夫随机场模型与近似贝叶斯计算方法的算法，但它采用零膨胀负二项分布来模拟数据信号。系统实验表明，相较于ZipHiC以及FastHiC、Juicer、HiCExplorer等其他方法，HiCPotts能够有效降低假阳性的发生率，并提高对真实染色质相互作用的检测效率。最重要的是，我们提供了相应的R/Bioconductor软件包，用户可利用零膨胀负二项分布或零膨胀泊松分布等不同模型来分析数据中的噪声与信号成分。  

可用性与实施方式：  
https://bioconductor.org/packages/HiCPotts/

我们此前开发了基于隐马尔可夫随机场模型与近似贝叶斯计算方法的ZipHiC，该算法利用零膨胀泊松分布来模拟数据中的噪声、真实信号与假阳性信号，结果表明这种方法能够有效识别Hi-C及micro-C数据中由DNA可及性、GC含量等因素引起的偏差。在此研究中，我们进一步提出了另一种基于相同模型的贝叶斯方法——HiCPotts，该方法改用零膨胀负二项分布来对数据进行分析。系统实验表明，与ZipHiC相比，HiCPotts能够有效降低假阳性的发生率，并提高真实相互作用的检测效率；同时，其性能也优于FastHiC、Juicer和HiCExplorer等其他方法。最重要的是，我们提供了相应的R/Bioconductor软件包，用户可利用零膨胀负二项分布或零膨胀泊松分布等不同模型对数据中的噪声、真实信号及假阳性信号进行建模分析。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Chromosome Conformation Capture methods, including Hi-C, micro-C or Capture-C, are used to map chromatin interactions genome-wide. Most of the existing computational methods do not account for sources of bias (such as DNA accessibility, GC content or TE content) in the data.

RESULTS: We previously developed ZipHiC, a Bayesian method based on the hidden Markov random field (HMRF) model and the Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC), that uses zero-inflated Poisson distribution to model the noise, signal and false signal of the data and showed that this approach was able to detect bias from DNA accessibility, GC content and TE content in both Hi-C and micro-C data. Here, we present HiCPotts, another Bayesian method based on the HMRF model and the ABC that uses a zero-inflated Negative Binomial distribution instead to model the noise and signal of the data. We systematically show that HiCPotts reduces false positives and increases recovery of true interactions compared to ZipHiC, but also compared to other methods such as FastHiC, Juicer and HiCExplorer. Most importantly, we provide an R/Bioconductor package that allows modelling the noise, signal and false signal using various distributions such as the zero-inflated Negative Binomial (ZINB) and the zero-inflated Poisson distribution (ZIP).

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: https://bioconductor.org/packages/HiCPotts/.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

all_papers.title: Causal Spectral Segmenter: Counterfactual Graph Reasoning for Weakly Supervised Pathology Segmentation
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Weakly supervised pathology segmentation aims to alleviate the reliance on costly pixel-level annotations, yet remains challenging due to severe tissue heterogeneity, complex morphological patterns, and strong contextual confounding in histopathology images. Existing transformer-based methods often learn spurious correlations between lesions and surrounding tissues, while graph-based approaches tend to suffer from feature over-smoothing, resulting in degraded boundary delineation and localization accuracy. Results To address these challenges, we propose a novel Causal Spectral Segmenter (CSS) for weakly supervised pathology segmentation. The proposed framework seamlessly integrates causal representation learning and multi-scale spectral graph reasoning. Specifically, a Causal Counterfactual Projector (CCP) is introduced to estimate lesion-specific causal effects through factual–counterfactual intervention, thereby suppressing contextual confounding and enhancing lesion-discriminative representations. Furthermore, we develop a Multi-scale Spectral Graph Reasoner (MSGR) composed of stacked Spectral Chebyshev Graph Convolution (SCGC) layers, which perform topology-aware spectral propagation across multiple neighborhood scales to capture long-range tissue dependencies while mitigating graph over-smoothing. By jointly modeling causal effects and multi-scale topological structures, CSS effectively improves lesion localization and boundary preservation under weak supervision. Extensive experiments on two public histopathology segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that CSS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods and achieves superior segmentation accuracy and structural consistency. Availability and Implementation The source code and implementation details will be publicly available at: https://github.com/zhangxu90s/CSS

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
在弱监督病理分割领域，虽然人们试图减少对昂贵像素级标注的依赖，但由于组织结构的异质性、复杂的形态特征以及组织病理图像中的强烈背景干扰，这一目标仍面临诸多挑战。现有的基于Transformer的方法往往会学习到病变与周围组织之间的虚假关联，而基于图论的方法则容易出现特征过度平滑的问题，从而导致边界划分和定位精度下降。  

**研究方法**  
为了解决这些难题，我们提出了一种新型的因果谱段分割算法——CSS。该框架将因果关系表示学习与多尺度谱图推理有机结合在一起：首先引入了因果反事实投影器（CCP），通过事实与反事实干预来估计病变特有的因果效应，从而有效抑制背景干扰并提升病变的区分能力；随后构建了由多层谱切比雪夫图卷积层组成的多尺度谱图推理器（MSGR），该机制能够在多个不同尺度上实现基于拓扑结构的谱传播，既能捕捉组织间的长距离依赖关系，又能避免特征过度平滑。通过同时建模因果效应与多尺度拓扑结构，CSS在弱监督环境下显著提升了病变的定位精度与边界保持能力。  

**实验验证**  
在两个公开发布的组织病理分割基准测试中，CSS的表现明显优于现有最先进方法，其分割精度与结构一致性均得到了显著提升。  

**代码与实现**  
我们的源代码及实现细节将公开发布在以下链接：  
https://github.com/zhangxu90s/CSS

all_papers.title: scMustree: a multi-scale functional hierarchy for single-cell transcriptomic analysis
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Resolving cellular heterogeneity requires methods that capture both discrete cell types and their functional relationships. Existing single-cell clustering approaches often produce flat partitions, limiting their ability to reveal rare cell states and continuous biological transitions. Here, we introduce scMustree, a computational framework that constructs a multi-scale hierarchy of single-cell transcriptomes, enabling integrated analysis of cellular organization and functional relationships. scMustree employs a top-down iterative decomposition to isolate transcriptionally homogeneous populations, followed by a bottom-up merging strategy guided by cluster-specific functional rankings—derived from differential expression and an isolation-forest-based scoring mechanism that quantifies functional distinctness. This unified approach captures lineage structures, functional similarities, and transitional states. Results Across 11 benchmark datasets, scMustree achieves competitive clustering accuracy while offering substantially enhanced biological interpretability. In diverse biological systems, it uncovers biologically consistent hierarchies and identifies previously uncharacterized cell states, including fibroblast and T-cell subsets in cancer and lipid-associated microglial populations in Alzheimer’s disease. By integrating structural and functional information, scMustree provides a scalable and biologically grounded framework for multi-resolution exploration of single-cell ecosystems, enabling discovery of rare and disease-relevant cell states across diverse biological contexts. Availability and implementation Freely available at Github( https://github.com/xuyp-csu/scMustree ) and Zenodo( https://zenodo.org/records/17480562 )

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
要理解细胞间的异质性，就必须同时捕捉不同的细胞类型及其功能关系。现有的单细胞聚类方法往往生成扁平的群体结构，这限制了它们揭示稀有细胞状态及连续生物学过程的能力。为此，我们提出了scMustree这一计算框架——该框架能够构建多尺度的单细胞转录组层次结构，从而实现细胞组织与功能关系的综合分析。scMustree首先采用自上而下的迭代分解方法分离出转录特征相似的细胞群体，随后通过自下而上的合并策略，结合基于差异表达数据得出的簇特异性功能排序结果，以及一种能够量化功能差异性的评分机制，最终形成完整的层次结构。这种统一的方法有效揭示了细胞的谱系关系、功能相似性及过渡状态。  

**实验结果**  
在11个基准数据集上的测试表明，scMustree不仅具有较高的聚类准确率，其生物学解释性也得到了显著提升。在多种生物系统中，该工具均能揭示出具有生物学意义的层次结构，并识别出此前未被描述的细胞类型——例如癌症中的成纤维细胞和T细胞亚群，以及阿尔茨海默病中与脂质相关的小胶质细胞群体。通过整合结构信息与功能数据，scMustree为多尺度探索单细胞生态系统提供了可扩展且基于生物学原理的分析工具，有助于在多种生物背景下发现稀有或与疾病相关的细胞状态。  

**开源与使用方式**  
scMustree已免费发布在Github（https://github.com/xuyp-csu/scMustree）和Zenodo（https://zenodo.org/records/17480562）平台上，可供大家自由下载和使用。

all_papers.title: Phys-AbGAT: A Physics-Informed Multi-Task Graph Attention Network for Robust Antibody-Antigen Binding Affinity Prediction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity is essential for therapeutic antibody design. Existing methods often model the dissociation constant (KD) and Gibbs free energy (ΔG) independently, overlooking their thermodynamic relationship and complex paratope-epitope spatial interactions. Results We introduce Phys-AbGAT, a physics-informed multi-task graph attention network that represents the antibody-antigen interface as a spatial graph. It integrates ESM2 evolutionary embeddings with radial basis functions and employs a thermodynamically motivated auxiliary loss to encourage coupling between log10⁡(KD) and ΔG. On an independent 42-complex benchmark, Phys-AbGAT achieved Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.569 for log10⁡(KD) and 0.573 for ΔG. In matched-set comparisons, Phys-AbGAT achieved numerically lower RMSE and higher PCC than four baseline methods. The differences remained significant after Holm correction for MVSF-AB and PPA-Pred2, but not for AREA-AFFINITY or CSM-AB. Higher attention scores were assigned to several aromatic paratope residues, providing model-level hypotheses for structural inspection. These results support Phys-AbGAT as an interpretable multi-task geometric framework for joint prediction of two affinity-related quantities. Availability and implementation Code and data are available at https://github.com/cliffgao/Phys-AbGAT

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Accurate prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity is essential for therapeutic antibody design. Existing methods often model the dissociation constant (KD) and Gibbs free energy (ΔG) independently, overlooking their thermodynamic relationship and complex paratope-epitope spatial interactions. Results We introduce Phys-AbGAT, a physics-informed multi-task graph attention network that represents the antibody-antigen interface as a spatial graph. It integrates ESM2 evolutionary embeddings with radial basis functions and employs a thermodynamically motivated auxiliary loss to encourage coupling between log10⁡(KD) and ΔG. On an independent 42-complex benchmark, Phys-AbGAT achieved Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.569 for log10⁡(KD) and 0.573 for ΔG. In matched-set comparisons, Phys-AbGAT achieved numerically lower RMSE and higher PCC than four baseline methods. The differences remained significant after Holm correction for MVSF-AB and PPA-Pred2, but not for AREA-AFFINITY or CSM-AB. Higher attention scores were assigned to several aromatic paratope residues, providing model-level hypotheses for structural inspection. These results support Phys-AbGAT as an interpretable multi-task geometric framework for joint prediction of two affinity-related quantities.

all_papers.title: Partaker: deep-learning-based single-cell-resolution analysis of multi-dimensional, long-term, microfluidic-based time-lapse microscopy data
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Deep-learning segmentation models for microbial time-lapse fluorescence microscopy already exist, but they are often difficult to use consistently across experiments and are not packaged with unified workflows for combining models, quantifying multi-channel fluorescence, and scaling analyses to large microfluidic imaging datasets. Results To address these challenges, we developed Partaker, an easy-to-use Python-based graphical tool for deep-learning segmentation, multi-channel fluorescence quantification, and morphological analysis of microbial cells over time. Partaker supports extensible model integration, efficient handling of large imaging datasets, and interactive visualization, enabling time-resolved analysis of population fluorescence distributions from per-cell measurements. We demonstrate performance using a two-strain validation experiment (housekeeping and inducible) and show robust recovery of population-level fluorescence dynamics with single-cell resolution. Availability and implementation Partaker is implemented in Python and is available on GitHub ( https://github.com/SamOliveiraLab/partaker ). A versioned release of the software is archived on Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18844425 ). Documentation, example datasets, and installation instructions are provided in the repository

all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Designing mRNA coding sequences that simultaneously optimize RNA accessibility in the translation initiation region and codon adaptation while preserving the encoded protein requires navigating a vast discrete combinatorial space. The inherently discrete nature of codon choices prevents direct application of gradient-based optimization, despite the availability of accurate deep learning predictors such as DeepRaccess for RNA accessibility prediction. Results We present the Input Data Differentiable Designer (ID3), a unified framework for mRNA codon optimization. ID3 treats trained models as fixed differentiable functions and optimizes input data through continuous probability distributions while preserving the encoded amino acid sequence through three constraint mechanisms. The framework shows strong performance in both accessibility optimization and joint accessibility-CAI optimization across diverse protein targets. We also provide convergence analyses from the perspective of trained model input optimization.
